comment: The Python decision functions of the per-answer ownership test (kb-10d; manage-agents reviews/lean-ownership-baseline-20261112.md section 2, criterion 1): an answer of a frozen key counts as Lean-decided only if none of these ran while it was answered (tools/ownership_trace.py). One owner: this file is the only list. A Python function of ve/ that computes a verdict, a selection, an outcome or a conflict status and is not listed here is a review finding. `qualname` matches the function and every function nested in it (`<qualname>.<locals>.…`); `methods: true` matches every method of the class (`<qualname>.<name>`), not the class body that runs once at import. ve/softnorms.py: since kb-10b no function of its own computes a status on the Lean path; its two Python paths (`SoftenedNormDocument.selected_rules` and `outcome_at` for a document built without its soft source) run `NormDocument.selected_rules`, `NormDocument.outcome` and `_Evaluator`, listed here, so they are caught through them.

functions.reason: builds each rule's selection formula of a hard or softened norm document (the selection Lean's soft-selected now owns)
builds a regulated predicate's completed outcome formula
expands derived predicates in selection and outcome formulas (the base-expanded formulas Lean's circ owns)
Python's path for which rules are selected at a tuple of a model (SoftenedNormDocument.selected_rules relays to Lean instead when it has its soft source)
computes the conflict targets (which rule pairs and tuples a conflict check must cover)
Python's conflict decision: targets, witness check and target proofs, with no Lean verdict
Python's private formula evaluator: computes a formula's truth value in a finite model
